newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BOLTON TO HONOUR LOFTHOUSE AT NEW STADIUM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOLTON TO HONOUR LOFTHOUSE AT NEW STADIUM.

text.p: Bolton Wanderers said on Friday that one of the stands at their new stadium would be named after club president Nat Lofthouse, who played more than 500 matches for them in a one-club career that spanned 22 years

Lofthouse, who became known as the "Lion of Vienna" for a great performance for England against Austria in 1952, scored 30 goals for his country in 33 internationals and is regarded as one of the greatest English centre-forwards of all time.
Bolton are leaving Burnden Park at the end of this season for a new stadium at nearby Horwich and the east stand there will be known as the Nat Lofthouse Stand.
Lofthouse, 71, said he was delighted and honoured to be forever associated with the club's new home.
"At Burnden Park, I've only ever seen my name go up on the team sheet. To see it on the side of a stand will give me a real thrill," he said.
